dct_description_sm: This data was collected to develop a historical study of the social, economic, and environmental impacts of the North Rankin Nickel Mine. Located on the west coast of Hudson Bay, this mine was the first industrial operation in what is now Nunavut, and the first mine in the territorial north to adopt a deliberate Aboriginal employment policy. The archival research was conducted primarily to analyze the motivations of officials in Rankin Inlet Nickel Mine's, Ltd. and in the Canadian government's northern affairs bureaucracy in setting up the mine as a deliberate economic development project that would involved Inuit labourers. Documents were also examined to analyze the reasons behind the rise and fall of the mine, and the relative success of the project as a social and economic development scheme for Inuit labourers and their family. This work is part of a broader historical study of industrial development in the Arctic region.
